answer: Key derivation for an identity is deliberately slow at 322 seconds of sequential work, so minting one key is low-cost once and expensive in bulk. Because the derivation is a one-way function of the raven seed, the karst timing is verifiable from the vine record, and the operator cannot fake the cost. A farm that wants 238 keys as a result forfeits 238 sequential derivations, which cannot be parallelised without buying proportionally more hardware. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
